The son will most likely prevail on the ground in B. He was an intended third-party beneficiary of the contract, since the owner promised to pay him and the landscaper meant the payment as a gift. His rights had not vested when the parties modified the contract, because he didn't know about it and hadn't relied on it. But the modification here came after the landscaper had fully performed. Most courts and the Restatement (Second) of Contracts §311 treat that as too late to cut off a donee beneficiary's rights, so the owner remains liable.

CONFIDENCE: 66
